changes.note: Working architecture proposal only. Accepted Identity, Structure, Book, relations and prose remain unchanged. Any real downstream impact needs the existing source-backed impact/revision workflows.

changed_components.title: Governing summary
changed_components.before: The Spring Ledger, working construction W (noncanonical; not author-approved). Built on the original 30-Book architecture (PR #551), which it does not modify. It keeps the original identity, the three co-governing engines (Ledger, Source, Old Hand) and the five arcs. Books 1-15 keep the original's events. The working construction corrects one thing in them: Book 1 reads the share-marks as evidence, and the first partial reading of the script is Book 8. It also states two things the original left implicit: the Hollow Gate, and the status of the stewardship tally. Arc IV (Books 19-22) is constructed as two conflicts. The Counted Rota: a lineage's channel repair gives it a Special Draw Right, and hand-light share-holders have draw converted in proportion to the hands they cannot return. Two Practices, One Gate: the counted Turn and the gift practice contest the Hollow Gate, and a rotating Gate Table sets its schedule with no authority over the record. Book 23 inherits genuine but seasonal abundance, drawn unevenly by the best-handed houses, and a belief that abundance needs no work. Book 30 is the Long Return, a deep-store pulse that needs channel labour and a gate routing, which are the two exports of Arc IV. Three finale mechanisms are held open for author choice: A (noncoercive mutual dependence), B (allotted binding rota under a bounded authority) and C (ratified trigger, the agent-proposed working direction for testing and not chosen). Whether shared accounting binds, the flood, the Compact's fate and the stance toward reform are not decided here.

changed_components.title: Stone Hall (Reckoners)
changed_components.before: Hereditary keepers of the Ledger. Under this working path the Hall dissolves in Book 5, and a remnant under Keeper Corrow continues as a dissenting institution. Typed as other because v2 has no institution category.
changed_components.after: Hereditary keepers of the Ledger. Under this working path the Hall splits in Book 5, as the original has it, and a remnant under Keeper Corrow continues as a dissenting institution. Typed as other because v2 has no institution category.

changed_components.title: The Hollow Gate
changed_components.before: The sluice that divides the high cistern's release between the upper and lower channels. The Council has set its schedule since the Turn. In the Book 15 trial the schedule carried release to the lower channels, and the high cistern showed surfeit. The construction reads the surfeit as that release's effect, which the original does not name. The schedule is the object of the Book 21 conflict.
changed_components.after: The sluice that divides the high cistern's release between the upper and lower channels. The Council has set its schedule since the Turn. In the Book 15 trial the high cistern showed surfeit, which the original defines as too much return, or stored water with no draw. The construction assumes that the trial's uncounted return labour fed the high channels beyond the Turn's count, so stored water rose with no draw to match it. Release draws the cistern down and cannot raise it. The schedule is the object of the Book 21 conflict.

changed_components.title: The counted Turn (high terraces)
changed_components.before: Draw matched to labour in the high terraces, run by the Council since the Turn in Book 6. The stewardship tally, from Book 15, is kept as a record of care for this practice. It holds the high cistern against surfeit.
changed_components.after: Labour matched to shares in the high terraces, run by the Council since the Turn in Book 6: each share returns labour by rota, and draw still follows shares. The counted Turn's labour holds the high cistern against surfeit. The stewardship tally, from Book 15, records that labour as a record of care for this practice; it does not hold the water.

changed_components.title: Settled Water
changed_components.before: Co-governance. Ledger, Source and Old Hand share the field, and no single engine dominates. Both conflicts come from settled practice, not from a new antagonist. Conflict A is unequal capacity to maintain shared channels. It makes hands set part of draw for the first time since Book 6, and it gives lineage crews a claim on draw. Conflict B is two proven practices, the counted Turn and the gift practice, which contest one outlet. The valley answers with a Gate Table that sets the schedule and holds no record. | Reader experience: warmth of shared repair; the cost of counting | Transition: Water is partly earned by hands. The Gate Table, the Special Draw Right and an ambiguous tally pass to the next generation.
changed_components.after: Co-governance. Ledger, Source and Old Hand share the field, and no single engine dominates. Both conflicts come from settled practice, not from a new antagonist. Conflict A is unequal capacity to maintain shared channels. It makes hands set part of draw for the first time in the series, and it gives lineage crews a claim on draw. Conflict B is two proven practices, the counted Turn and the gift practice, which contest one outlet. The valley answers with a Gate Table that sets the schedule and holds no record. | Reader experience: warmth of shared repair; the cost of counting | Transition: Water is partly earned by hands. The Gate Table, the Special Draw Right and an ambiguous tally pass to the next generation.

changed_components.title: Unmeasured
changed_components.before: The Source is the physical deadline. The Long Return is a deep-store pulse, predicted by the Balance Stones from Book 23. It needs two things Arc IV left the valley: channel labour, which is hands, and a Gate schedule that routes the surge. Books 23-26 carry the Brightwater generation's inheritance. Books 27-29 carry the Compact's bid and, under Alternative C, the ratification window. Book 30 chooses among three mechanisms. A is noncoercive mutual dependence, in which care is counted and nothing is owed. B is an allotted binding rota under a lot-drawn, time-limited Table, with grain-labour from the Compact. C is a ratified trigger that activates B's rule only when a published threshold is crossed. The original's three options map onto these: the single measured Turn is B without its guards, and the Compact's settlement is a clause of B or C. No option restores the Stone Hall's sole custody. | Reader experience: hope that is earned by cost; wonder at the deepest chamber | Transition: The series closes locally. A shared practice and the long-range questions continue.
